title: Selected Topics in Differential Geometry in Biophysics and Medical Physics: A Review of Five Domains
content: Biological morphology, molecular mechanics, medical image analysis, and physiological wave propagation frequently obey constraints that are intrinsically geometric rather than Euclidean. This article develops a unified geometric perspective across five selected domains of continuum biophysics and clinical medical physics. First, we explore extrinsic surface geometry, Canham–Helfrich and area-difference elasticity, and Gauss–Bonnet topological barriers in lipid membranes and viral scission. Second, we examine principal \(\mathrm{SO}(3)\) Cosserat frame bundles, twist connections, and the Călugăreanu–White–Fuller theorem in DNA supercoiling and isoform-specific topoisomerase pharmacology. Third, we cover the Cartan–Hadamard symmetric space \(\mathrm{Sym}^+(3) \cong \mathrm{GL}(3,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{O}(3)\), Log-Euclidean similarity geometry, and multi-fiber spherical extensions in Diffusion MRI and neurosurgical tractography. Fourth, we discuss infinite-dimensional Sobolev metrics on diffeomorphism groups \(\mathrm{Diff}_V(\Omega)\), Euler–Poincaré (EPDiff) geodesic flows, and differential-form dose accumulation in computational anatomy and four-dimensional adaptive radiotherapy. Finally, we address principal gauge connections, Pancharatnam–Berry geometric phases, and topological phase defects in low-Reynolds-number motility, adiabatic MRI pulse design, and cardiac arrhythmia mapping. Alongside pedagogical derivations (collected in technical appendices), we critically compare competing physical models, evaluate numerical discretization pitfalls, uncertainty quantification, and phantom/clinical validation benchmarks, and clarify where idealized geometric invariants must be tempered by physiological dynamics and clinical trial evidence.
